exposure: Antepartum surgery vs. surgery during cesarean section
outcome: Benign vs. malignant status of the mass
cohort: 53 pregnant women with adnexal masses (other than non-gynecological mass and ectopic pregnancy) from 11,000 pregnancy cases referred to the Qaem Hospital in the Mashhad University of Medical Sciences, Iran, between 2010 and 2014
finding: The rate of malignant tumors was considerably higher in women who had antepartum mass excision compared to those with mass resection during CS, and tumors were larger and more complex in patients who had antepartum surgery.
mod_finding: The study found that adnexal masses removed during cesarean section were less likely to be malignant compared to those removed antepartum.
